raft_max_buffered_follower_append_entrie.name: raft_max_buffered_follower_append_entries_bytes_per_shard
raft_max_buffered_follower_append_entrie.description: The total size of append entry requests that may be cached per shard, using the Raft-buffered protocol. When an entry is cached, the leader can continue serving requests because the ordering of the cached requests cannot change. When the total size of cached requests reaches the set limit, back pressure is applied to throttle producers.

raft_max_inflight_follower_append_entrie.name: raft_max_inflight_follower_append_entries_requests_per_shard
raft_max_inflight_follower_append_entrie.description: The maximum number of append entry requests that may be sent from Raft groups on a Seastar shard to the current node, and are awaiting a reply. This property replaces `raft_max_concurrent_append_requests_per_follower`.

raft_max_recovery_memory.name: raft_max_recovery_memory
raft_max_recovery_memory.description: Maximum memory that can be used for reads in Raft recovery process by default 15% of total memory.

raft_recovery_concurrency_per_shard.name: raft_recovery_concurrency_per_shard
raft_recovery_concurrency_per_shard.description: Number of partitions that may simultaneously recover data to a particular shard. This number is limited to avoid overwhelming nodes when they come back online after an outage.

raft_recovery_throttle_disable_dynamic_m.name: raft_recovery_throttle_disable_dynamic_mode
raft_recovery_throttle_disable_dynamic_m.description:
Disables cross shard sharing used to throttle recovery traffic. Should only be used to debug unexpected problems.

include::reference:partial$internal-use-property.adoc[]

raft_replica_max_flush_delay_ms.name: raft_replica_max_flush_delay_ms
raft_replica_max_flush_delay_ms.description: Maximum delay between two subsequent flushes. After this delay, the log is automatically force flushed.

raft_replica_max_pending_flush_bytes.name: raft_replica_max_pending_flush_bytes
raft_replica_max_pending_flush_bytes.description: Maximum number of bytes that are not flushed per partition. If the configured threshold is reached, the log is automatically flushed even if it has not been explicitly requested.

raft_replicate_batch_window_size.name: raft_replicate_batch_window_size
raft_replicate_batch_window_size.description: Maximum size of requests cached for replication.

raft_smp_max_non_local_requests.name: raft_smp_max_non_local_requests
raft_smp_max_non_local_requests.description: Maximum number of cross-core (inter-shard communication) requests pending in Raft's Seastar SMP group. For details, see the Seastar `smp_service_group` documentation at https://docs.seastar.io/master/.

raft_timeout_now_timeout_ms.name: raft_timeout_now_timeout_ms
raft_timeout_now_timeout_ms.description: Timeout for Raft's timeout_now RPC. This RPC is used to force a follower to dispatch a round of votes immediately.

raft_transfer_leader_recovery_timeout_ms.name: raft_transfer_leader_recovery_timeout_ms
raft_transfer_leader_recovery_timeout_ms.description: Follower recovery timeout waiting period when transferring leadership.

readers_cache_eviction_timeout_ms.name: readers_cache_eviction_timeout_ms
readers_cache_eviction_timeout_ms.description: Duration after which inactive readers are evicted from cache.

readers_cache_target_max_size.name: readers_cache_target_max_size
readers_cache_target_max_size.description: Maximum desired number of readers cached per NTP. This a soft limit, meaning that a number of readers in cache may temporarily increase as cleanup is performed in the background.

reclaim_batch_cache_min_free.name: reclaim_batch_cache_min_free
reclaim_batch_cache_min_free.description: Minimum amount of free memory maintained by the batch cache background reclaimer.

reclaim_growth_window.name: reclaim_growth_window
reclaim_growth_window.description: Starting from the last point in time when memory was reclaimed from the batch cache, this is the duration during which the amount of memory to reclaim grows at a significant rate, based on heuristics about the amount of available memory.

reclaim_stable_window.name: reclaim_stable_window
reclaim_stable_window.description: If the duration since the last time memory was reclaimed is longer than the amount of time specified in this property, the memory usage of the batch cache is considered stable, so only the minimum size (`reclaim_min_size`) is set to be reclaimed.

recovery_mode_enabled.name: recovery_mode_enabled
recovery_mode_enabled.description: If `true`, start Redpanda in recovery mode, where user partitions are not loaded and only administrative operations are allowed.

redpanda.cloud_topic.enabled.name: redpanda.cloud_topic.enabled
redpanda.cloud_topic.enabled.description: Enable Cloud Topic storage mode for this topic. When enabled, topic data is stored primarily in object storage with local storage used only as a write buffer.

redpanda.iceberg.delete.name: redpanda.iceberg.delete
redpanda.iceberg.delete.description: Whether the corresponding Iceberg table is deleted upon deleting the topic.

redpanda.iceberg.invalid.record.action.name: redpanda.iceberg.invalid.record.action
redpanda.iceberg.invalid.record.action.description: Whether to write invalid records to a dead-letter queue (DLQ).

redpanda.iceberg.mode.name: redpanda.iceberg.mode
redpanda.iceberg.mode.description: Enable the Iceberg integration for the topic and control how Redpanda translates records into the Iceberg table. Set one of the modes (`disabled`, `key_value`, `value_schema_id_prefix`, or `value_schema_latest`), or use the section-based syntax to independently configure key, value, and header translation.

redpanda.iceberg.partition.spec.name: redpanda.iceberg.partition.spec
redpanda.iceberg.partition.spec.description: The link:https://iceberg.apache.org/docs/nightly/partitioning/[partitioning^] specification for the Iceberg table.

redpanda.iceberg.target.lag.ms.name: redpanda.iceberg.target.lag.ms
redpanda.iceberg.target.lag.ms.description: Controls how often the data in the Iceberg table is refreshed with new data from the topic. Redpanda attempts to commit all data produced to the topic within the lag target, subject to resource availability.

redpanda.key.schema.id.validation.name: redpanda.key.schema.id.validation
redpanda.key.schema.id.validation.description: Enable validation of the schema ID for keys on a record. When enabled, Redpanda validates that the schema ID encoded in the record's key is registered in the Schema Registry according to the configured subject name strategy.

redpanda.key.subject.name.strategy.name: redpanda.key.subject.name.strategy
redpanda.key.subject.name.strategy.description: The subject name strategy for keys when `redpanda.key.schema.id.validation` is enabled. This determines how the topic and schema are mapped to a subject name in the Schema Registry.

redpanda.leaders.preference.name: redpanda.leaders.preference
redpanda.leaders.preference.description:
The preferred location (rack) for partition leaders of a topic.

This property inherits the value from the prop:default_leaders_preference[link=true] cluster configuration property. You may override the cluster-wide setting by specifying the value for individual topics.

If the cluster configuration property prop:enable_rack_awareness[link=true] is set to `false`, Leader Pinning is disabled across the cluster.

redpanda.remote.delete.name: redpanda.remote.delete
redpanda.remote.delete.description: A flag that enables deletion of data from object storage for Tiered Storage when it's deleted from local storage for a topic.

redpanda.remote.read.name: redpanda.remote.read
redpanda.remote.read.description: A flag for enabling Redpanda to fetch data for a topic from object storage to local storage. When set to `true` together with `redpanda.remote.write`, it enables the Tiered Storage feature.

redpanda.remote.readreplica.name: redpanda.remote.readreplica
redpanda.remote.readreplica.description:
The name of the object storage bucket for a Remote Read Replica topic.

ifdef::env-cloud[]
Remote Read Replicas are available on BYOC clusters only.
endif::[]

redpanda.remote.recovery.name: redpanda.remote.recovery
redpanda.remote.recovery.description: A flag that enables the recovery or reproduction of a topic from object storage for Tiered Storage. The recovered data is saved in local storage, and the maximum amount of recovered data is determined by the local storage retention limits of the topic.

redpanda.remote.write.name: redpanda.remote.write
redpanda.remote.write.description: A flag for enabling Redpanda to upload data for a topic from local storage to object storage. When set to `true` together with `redpanda.remote.read`, it enables the Tiered Storage feature.

redpanda.schema.registry.context.name: redpanda.schema.registry.context
redpanda.schema.registry.context.description: The Schema Registry context Redpanda uses to resolve the schemas for records in this topic, for example when translating the topic to an Iceberg table. Defaults to the Schema Registry default context (`.`).

redpanda.storage.mode.name: redpanda.storage.mode
redpanda.storage.mode.description:
The storage mode for a topic. Determines how topic data is stored and whether it is eligible for upload to object storage.

Accepted values:

* `local`: Topic data is stored only on the broker's local disk. Object storage upload is disabled for the topic, regardless of cluster-level Tiered Storage settings.
* `tiered`: Topic data is stored on local disk and also uploaded to object storage. Enables Tiered Storage for the topic.
* `cloud`: Topic data is stored in object storage using the Cloud Topics architecture. Local storage is used only as a write buffer.
* `unset`: Specifies that the topic's storage mode is unset, regardless of the cluster default. The topic may still have Tiered Storage enabled through the legacy properties `redpanda.remote.read` and `redpanda.remote.write`.

Starting in Redpanda v26.2, the `tiered` value is an alias that resolves to Tiered Storage v1 or v2 when the topic is created, according to the prop:default_redpanda_storage_mode_tiered_impl[link=true] cluster property. The resolved version is reported by the read-only `redpanda.storage.mode.impl` property, and the storage mode of a topic displays as `tiered` for both versions.

This property overrides the cluster-wide prop:default_redpanda_storage_mode[link=true] setting for individual topics.

redpanda.storage.mode.impl.name: redpanda.storage.mode.impl
redpanda.storage.mode.impl.description:
The exact implementation of the topic's storage mode. Topics with the `tiered` storage mode report `tiered_v1` (Tiered Storage v1) or `tiered_v2` (Tiered Storage v2); topics with other storage modes mirror the value of `redpanda.storage.mode`.

This property is read-only after topic creation. To select the Tiered Storage version for a topic explicitly, set this property together with a matching `redpanda.storage.mode` value when you create the topic (both `tiered_v1` and `tiered_v2` correspond to the `tiered` mode). You can omit `redpanda.storage.mode` only if this property matches the version selected by the cluster default. To change a topic's storage mode after creation, alter `redpanda.storage.mode` instead.

If this property is not set at topic creation, the `tiered` storage mode resolves to the version selected by the prop:default_redpanda_storage_mode_tiered_impl[link=true] cluster property.

redpanda.value.schema.id.validation.name: redpanda.value.schema.id.validation
redpanda.value.schema.id.validation.description: Enable validation of the schema ID for values on a record. When enabled, Redpanda validates that the schema ID encoded in the record's value is registered in the Schema Registry according to the configured subject name strategy.

redpanda.value.subject.name.strategy.name: redpanda.value.subject.name.strategy
redpanda.value.subject.name.strategy.description: The subject name strategy for values when `redpanda.value.schema.id.validation` is enabled. This determines how the topic and schema are mapped to a subject name in the Schema Registry.

release_cache_on_segment_roll.name: release_cache_on_segment_roll
release_cache_on_segment_roll.description: Flag for specifying whether or not to release cache when a full segment is rolled.

replicate_append_timeout_ms.name: replicate_append_timeout_ms
replicate_append_timeout_ms.description: Timeout for append entry requests issued while replicating entries.

replication.factor.name: replication.factor
replication.factor.description:
The number of replicas of a topic to save in different nodes (brokers) of a cluster.

If `replication.factor` is set to a positive value, it overrides the cluster property `default_topic_replications` for the topic.

ifdef::env-cloud[]
Redpanda Cloud clusters require a replication factor of at least 3; a lower value is rejected.
endif::[]

retention.bytes.name: retention.bytes
retention.bytes.description:
A size-based retention limit that configures the maximum size that a topic partition can grow before becoming eligible for cleanup.

If `retention.bytes` is set to a positive value, it overrides the cluster property `retention_bytes` for the topic, and the total retained size for the topic is `retention.bytes` multiplied by the number of partitions for the topic.

When both size-based (`retention.bytes`) and time-based (`retention.ms`) retention limits are set, cleanup occurs when either limit is reached.

This property supports three states:

* Positive value: Sets the maximum bytes per partition. When exceeded, oldest data becomes eligible for cleanup.
* 0: Partitions are immediately eligible for cleanup.
* Negative value: Disables size-based retention for this topic.

retention.local.target.bytes.name: retention.local.target.bytes
retention.local.target.bytes.description:
A size-based retention limit for Tiered Storage that configures the maximum size that a topic partition in local storage can grow before becoming eligible for cleanup. It applies per partition and is equivalent to `retention.bytes` without Tiered Storage.

This property supports three states:

* Positive value: Sets the maximum bytes per partition in local storage before cleanup.
* 0: Data in local storage is immediately eligible for cleanup.
* Negative value: Disables size-based local retention override for this topic.

retention.local.target.ms.name: retention.local.target.ms
retention.local.target.ms.description:
A time-based retention limit for Tiered Storage that sets the maximum duration that a log's segment file for a topic is retained in local storage before cleanup. It applies per partition and is equivalent to `retention.ms` without Tiered Storage.

This property supports three states:

* Positive value: Sets the maximum milliseconds to retain data in local storage.
* 0: Data in local storage is immediately eligible for cleanup.
* Negative value: Disables time-based local retention override for this topic.

retention.ms.name: retention.ms
retention.ms.description:
A time-based retention limit that configures the maximum duration that a log's segment file for a topic is retained before it becomes eligible to be cleaned up. To consume all data, a consumer of the topic must read from a segment before its `retention.ms` elapses, otherwise the segment may be compacted and/or deleted.

If `retention.ms` is set to a positive value, it overrides the cluster property `log_retention_ms` for the topic.

When both size-based (`retention.bytes`) and time-based (`retention.ms`) retention limits are set, the earliest occurring limit applies.

This property supports three states:

* Positive value: Sets the maximum milliseconds to retain data. After this duration, segments become eligible for cleanup.
* 0: Data is immediately eligible for cleanup.
* Negative value: Disables time-based retention for this topic.

retention_bytes.name: retention_bytes
retention_bytes.description:
Default maximum number of bytes per partition on disk before triggering deletion of the oldest messages. If `null` (the default value), no limit is applied.

The topic property `retention.bytes` overrides the value of `retention_bytes` at the topic level.

retention_local_strict.name: retention_local_strict
retention_local_strict.description: Flag to allow Tiered Storage topics to expand to consumable retention policy limits. When this flag is enabled, non-local retention settings are used, and local retention settings are used to inform data removal policies in low-disk space scenarios.

retention_local_strict_override.name: retention_local_strict_override
retention_local_strict_override.description: Trim log data when a cloud topic reaches its local retention limit. When this option is disabled Redpanda will allow partitions to grow past the local retention limit, and will be trimmed automatically as storage reaches the configured target size.

retention_local_target_bytes_default.name: retention_local_target_bytes_default
retention_local_target_bytes_default.description:
Local retention size target for partitions of topics with object storage write enabled. If `null`, the property is disabled.

This property can be overridden on a per-topic basis by setting `retention.local.target.bytes` in each topic enabled for Tiered Storage.

retention_local_target_capacity_bytes.name: retention_local_target_capacity_bytes
retention_local_target_capacity_bytes.description: The target capacity (in bytes) that log storage will try to use before additional retention rules take over to trim data to meet the target. When no target is specified, storage usage is unbounded.

retention_local_target_capacity_percent.name: retention_local_target_capacity_percent
retention_local_target_capacity_percent.description: The target capacity in percent of unreserved space (`disk_reservation_percent`) that log storage will try to use before additional retention rules will take over to trim data in order to meet the target. When no target is specified storage usage is unbounded.

retention_local_target_ms_default.name: retention_local_target_ms_default
retention_local_target_ms_default.description:
Local retention time target for partitions of topics with object storage write enabled.

This property can be overridden on a per-topic basis by setting `retention.local.target.ms` in each topic enabled for Tiered Storage.

retention_local_trim_interval.name: retention_local_trim_interval
retention_local_trim_interval.description: The period during which disk usage is checked for disk pressure, and data is optionally trimmed to meet the target.

retention_local_trim_overage_coeff.name: retention_local_trim_overage_coeff
retention_local_trim_overage_coeff.description: The space management control loop reclaims the overage multiplied by this this coefficient to compensate for data that is written during the idle period between control loop invocations.

retries.name: retries
retries.description: Number of times to retry a request to a broker.

retry_base_backoff_ms.name: retry_base_backoff_ms
retry_base_backoff_ms.description: Delay (in milliseconds) for initial retry backoff.

rpc_client_connections_per_peer.name: rpc_client_connections_per_peer
rpc_client_connections_per_peer.description: The maximum number of connections a broker will open to each of its peers.

rpc_server.name: rpc_server
rpc_server.description: IP address and port for the Remote Procedure Call (RPC) server.

rpc_server_compress_replies.name: rpc_server_compress_replies
rpc_server_compress_replies.description: Enable compression for internal RPC (remote procedure call) server replies.

rpc_server_listen_backlog.name: rpc_server_listen_backlog
rpc_server_listen_backlog.description: Maximum TCP connection queue length for Kafka server and internal RPC server. If `null` (the default value), no queue length is set.

rpc_server_tcp_recv_buf.name: rpc_server_tcp_recv_buf
rpc_server_tcp_recv_buf.description: Internal RPC TCP receive buffer size. If `null` (the default value), no buffer size is set by Redpanda.

rpc_server_tcp_send_buf.name: rpc_server_tcp_send_buf
rpc_server_tcp_send_buf.description: Internal RPC TCP send buffer size. If `null` (the default value), then no buffer size is set by Redpanda.

rpc_server_tls.name: rpc_server_tls
rpc_server_tls.description: TLS configuration for the RPC server.

rps_limit_acls_and_users_operations.name: rps_limit_acls_and_users_operations
rps_limit_acls_and_users_operations.description: Rate limit, in requests per second, for ACL and user operations on the controller. The controller processes cluster management requests (such as creating, deleting, and updating ACLs and users) through the controller log (raft0).

rps_limit_configuration_operations.name: rps_limit_configuration_operations
rps_limit_configuration_operations.description: Rate limit, in requests per second, for configuration operations on the controller. The controller processes cluster management requests (such as cluster configuration updates, feature activations, and data policy changes) through the controller log (raft0).

rps_limit_move_operations.name: rps_limit_move_operations
rps_limit_move_operations.description: Rate limit, in requests per second, for move operations on the controller. The controller processes cluster management requests (such as moving and canceling partition replica reassignments) through the controller log (raft0).

rps_limit_node_management_operations.name: rps_limit_node_management_operations
rps_limit_node_management_operations.description: Rate limit, in requests per second, for node management operations on the controller. The controller processes cluster management requests (such as decommissioning, recommissioning, and setting brokers to maintenance mode) through the controller log (raft0).

rps_limit_topic_operations.name: rps_limit_topic_operations
rps_limit_topic_operations.description: Rate limit, in requests per second, for topic operations on the controller. The controller processes cluster management requests (such as creating, deleting, and updating topics and partition counts) through the controller log (raft0).

sasl_kerberos_config.name: sasl_kerberos_config
sasl_kerberos_config.description: The location of the Kerberos `krb5.conf` file for Redpanda.

sasl_kerberos_keytab.name: sasl_kerberos_keytab
sasl_kerberos_keytab.description: The location of the Kerberos keytab file for Redpanda.

sasl_kerberos_principal.name: sasl_kerberos_principal
sasl_kerberos_principal.description: The primary of the Kerberos Service Principal Name (SPN) for Redpanda.

sasl_kerberos_principal_mapping.name: sasl_kerberos_principal_mapping
sasl_kerberos_principal_mapping.description: Rules for mapping Kerberos principal names to Redpanda user principals.

sasl_mechanism.name: sasl_mechanism
sasl_mechanism.description:
The SASL mechanism to use when the HTTP Proxy client connects to the Kafka API. These credentials are used when the HTTP Proxy API listener has `authentication_method`: `none` but the cluster requires authenticated access to the Kafka API. This property specifies which individual SASL mechanism the HTTP Proxy client should use, while the cluster-wide available mechanisms are configured using the `sasl_mechanisms` cluster property.

include::shared:partial$http-proxy-ephemeral-credentials-breaking-change.adoc[]

sasl_mechanisms.name: sasl_mechanisms
sasl_mechanisms.description: A list of supported SASL mechanisms, if no override is defined in `sasl_mechanisms_overrides` for each Kafka listener. Accepted values: `SCRAM`, `GSSAPI`, `OAUTHBEARER`, `PLAIN`.  Note that in order to enable PLAIN, you must also enable SCRAM.

sasl_mechanisms_overrides.name: sasl_mechanisms_overrides
sasl_mechanisms_overrides.description: Configure different SASL authentication mechanisms for specific listeners. This overrides the cluster-wide `sasl_mechanisms` setting for the specified listener. Use this when you need different authentication methods on different listeners, such as SCRAM for internal traffic and OAUTHBEARER for external clients. The same requirements from `sasl_mechanisms` apply.

schema_registry_always_normalize.name: schema_registry_always_normalize
schema_registry_always_normalize.description: Always normalize schemas. If set, this overrides the `normalize` parameter in requests to the Schema Registry API.

schema_registry_api.name: schema_registry_api
schema_registry_api.description: Schema Registry API listener address and port

schema_registry_api_tls.name: schema_registry_api_tls
schema_registry_api_tls.description: TLS configuration for Schema Registry API.

schema_registry_deferred_recovery.name: schema_registry_deferred_recovery
schema_registry_deferred_recovery.description: Defer schema compilation during Schema Registry startup, then compile the loaded schemas in parallel across cores. If disabled, every replayed record is compiled sequentially during the replay.

schema_registry_enable_authorization.name: schema_registry_enable_authorization
schema_registry_enable_authorization.description:
Enables ACL-based authorization for Schema Registry requests. When `true`, Schema Registry
uses ACL-based authorization instead of the default `public/user/superuser` authorization model.

schema_registry_enable_qualified_subject.name: schema_registry_enable_qualified_subjects
schema_registry_enable_qualified_subject.description: Enable parsing of qualified subject syntax (:.context:subject). When true, qualified syntax is parsed to extract context and subject. When false, subjects are treated literally, as subjects in the default context.

schema_registry_replay_on_startup.name: schema_registry_replay_on_startup
schema_registry_replay_on_startup.description: Replay the internal `_schemas` topic into the store at Schema Registry start-up instead of lazily on the first request. Makes recovery time predictable and keeps the first request from blocking behind a full replay.

schema_registry_replication_factor.name: schema_registry_replication_factor
schema_registry_replication_factor.description: Replication factor for internal `_schemas` topic. If unset, defaults to the `default_topic_replications` cluster property.

schema_registry_sync_memory_bytes.name: schema_registry_sync_memory_bytes
schema_registry_sync_memory_bytes.description: Maximum bytes of schema bodies held in memory at once while a schema registry cluster link reconciles from the source.

schema_registry_sync_parallelism.name: schema_registry_sync_parallelism
schema_registry_sync_parallelism.description: Maximum number of schemas imported concurrently while a schema registry cluster link reconciles from the source.

schema_registry_use_rpc.name: schema_registry_use_rpc
schema_registry_use_rpc.description: Use internal Redpanda RPCs for schema registry internal topic I/O. When disabled, use a Kafka client for schema registry internal topic I/O instead.

scram_password.description:

seed_servers.name: seed_servers
seed_servers.description:
List of the seed servers used to join current cluster. If the `seed_servers` list is empty the broker will be a cluster root and it will form a new cluster.

* When `empty_seed_starts_cluster` is `true`, Redpanda enables one broker with an empty `seed_servers` list to initiate a new cluster. The broker with an empty `seed_servers` becomes the cluster root, to which other brokers must connect to join the cluster. Brokers looking to join the cluster should have their `seed_servers` populated with the cluster root's address, facilitating their connection to the cluster.
* When `empty_seed_starts_cluster` is `false`, Redpanda requires all brokers to start with a known set of brokers listed in `seed_servers`. The `seed_servers` list must not be empty and should be identical across these initial seed brokers, containing the addresses of all seed brokers. Brokers not included in the `seed_servers` list use it to discover and join the cluster, allowing for expansion beyond the foundational members.

segment.bytes.name: segment.bytes
segment.bytes.description:
The maximum size of an active log segment for a topic. When the size of an active segment exceeds `segment.bytes`, the segment is closed and a new active segment is created. The closed, inactive segment is then eligible to be cleaned up according to retention properties.

When `segment.bytes` is set to a positive value, it overrides the cluster property:

* `log_segment_size` for non-compacted topics
* `compacted_log_segment_size` for compacted topics (when `cleanup.policy=compact`)

segment.ms.name: segment.ms
segment.ms.description:
The maximum duration that a log segment of a topic is active (open for writes and not deletable). A periodic event, with `segment.ms` as its period, forcibly closes the active segment and transitions, or rolls, to a new active segment. The closed (inactive) segment is then eligible to be cleaned up according to cleanup and retention properties.

If set to a positive duration, `segment.ms` overrides the cluster property `log_segment_ms`. Values are automatically clamped between the cluster bounds set by `log_segment_ms_min` (default: 10 minutes) and `log_segment_ms_max` (default: 1 year). If your configured value exceeds these bounds, Redpanda uses the bound value and logs a warning. Check current cluster bounds with `rpk cluster config get log_segment_ms_min log_segment_ms_max`.

For topics with compaction enabled, `max.compaction.lag.ms` also acts as a limit to `segment.ms`.

This property supports three states:

* Positive value: Sets the maximum milliseconds a segment remains active before rolling to a new segment.
* 0: Segments are immediately eligible for closure.
* Negative value: Disables time-based segment rolling for this topic.

segment_appender_flush_timeout_ms.name: segment_appender_flush_timeout_ms
segment_appender_flush_timeout_ms.description: Maximum delay until buffered data is written.

shadow_link_failover_batch_size.name: shadow_link_failover_batch_size
shadow_link_failover_batch_size.description: Maximum number of mirror topics to include in a single batched failover controller command.

space_management_enable.name: space_management_enable
space_management_enable.description: Option to explicitly disable automatic disk space management. If this property was explicitly disabled while using v23.2, it will remain disabled following an upgrade.

space_management_max_log_concurrency.name: space_management_max_log_concurrency
space_management_max_log_concurrency.description: Maximum parallel logs inspected during space management process.

space_management_max_segment_concurrency.name: space_management_max_segment_concurrency
space_management_max_segment_concurrency.description: Maximum parallel segments inspected during space management process.

storage_compaction_index_memory.name: storage_compaction_index_memory
storage_compaction_index_memory.description: Maximum number of bytes that may be used on each shard by compaction index writers.

storage_compaction_key_map_memory.name: storage_compaction_key_map_memory
storage_compaction_key_map_memory.description: Maximum number of bytes that may be used on each shard by compaction key-offset maps. Only applies when `log_compaction_use_sliding_window` is set to `true`.

storage_compaction_key_map_memory_limit_.name: storage_compaction_key_map_memory_limit_percent
storage_compaction_key_map_memory_limit_.description: Limit on `storage_compaction_key_map_memory`, expressed as a percentage of memory per shard, that bounds the amount of memory used by compaction key-offset maps.

storage_failure_injection_config_path.name: storage_failure_injection_config_path
storage_failure_injection_config_path.description: Path to the configuration file used for low level storage failure injection.

storage_failure_injection_enabled.name: storage_failure_injection_enabled
storage_failure_injection_enabled.description: If `true`, inject low level storage failures on the write path. Do _not_ use for production instances.

storage_ignore_cstore_hints.name: storage_ignore_cstore_hints
storage_ignore_cstore_hints.description: When set, cstore hints are ignored and not used for data access (but are otherwise generated).

storage_ignore_timestamps_in_future_sec.name: storage_ignore_timestamps_in_future_sec
storage_ignore_timestamps_in_future_sec.description:
The maximum number of seconds that a record's timestamp can be ahead of a Redpanda broker's clock and still be used when deciding whether to clean up the record for data retention. This property makes possible the timely cleanup of records from clients with clocks that are drastically unsynchronized relative to Redpanda.

When determining whether to clean up a record with timestamp more than `storage_ignore_timestamps_in_future_sec` seconds ahead of the broker, Redpanda ignores the record's timestamp and instead uses a valid timestamp of another record in the same segment, or (if another record's valid timestamp is unavailable) the timestamp of when the segment file was last modified (mtime).

By default, `storage_ignore_timestamps_in_future_sec` is disabled (null).

storage_max_concurrent_replay.name: storage_max_concurrent_replay
storage_max_concurrent_replay.description: Maximum number of partitions' logs that will be replayed concurrently at startup, or flushed concurrently on shutdown.

storage_min_free_bytes.name: storage_min_free_bytes
storage_min_free_bytes.description: Threshold of minimum bytes free space before rejecting producers.

storage_read_buffer_size.name: storage_read_buffer_size
storage_read_buffer_size.description: Size of each read buffer (one per in-flight read, per log segment).

storage_read_readahead_count.name: storage_read_readahead_count
storage_read_readahead_count.description: How many additional reads to issue ahead of current read location.

storage_reserve_min_segments.name: storage_reserve_min_segments
storage_reserve_min_segments.description: The number of segments per partition that the system will attempt to reserve disk capacity for. For example, if the maximum segment size is configured to be 100 MB, and the value of this option is 2, then in a system with 10 partitions Redpanda will attempt to reserve at least 2 GB of disk space.

storage_space_alert_free_threshold_bytes.name: storage_space_alert_free_threshold_bytes
storage_space_alert_free_threshold_bytes.description: Threshold of minimum bytes free space before setting storage space alert.

storage_space_alert_free_threshold_perce.name: storage_space_alert_free_threshold_percent
storage_space_alert_free_threshold_perce.description: Threshold of minimum percent free space before setting storage space alert.

storage_strict_data_init.name: storage_strict_data_init
storage_strict_data_init.description: Requires that an empty file named `.redpanda_data_dir` be present in the broker configuration `data_directory`. If set to `true`, Redpanda will refuse to start if the file is not found in the data directory.

storage_target_replay_bytes.name: storage_target_replay_bytes
storage_target_replay_bytes.description: Target bytes to replay from disk on startup after clean shutdown: controls frequency of snapshots and checkpoints.

tls_certificate_name_format.name: tls_certificate_name_format
tls_certificate_name_format.description: The format of the certificates's distinguished name to use for mTLS principal mapping. The `legacy` format would appear as 'C=US,ST=California,L=San Francisco,O=Redpanda,CN=redpanda', while the `rfc2253` format would appear as 'CN=redpanda,O=Redpanda,L=San Francisco,ST=California,C=US'.

tls_enable_renegotiation.name: tls_enable_renegotiation
tls_enable_renegotiation.description: TLS client-initiated renegotiation is considered unsafe and is by default disabled.  Only re-enable it if you are experiencing issues with your TLS-enabled client.  This option has no effect on TLSv1.3 connections as client-initiated renegotiation was removed.

tls_min_version.name: tls_min_version
tls_min_version.description: The minimum TLS version that Redpanda clusters support. This property prevents client applications from negotiating a downgrade to the TLS version when they make a connection to a Redpanda cluster.

tls_v1_2_cipher_suites.name: tls_v1_2_cipher_suites
tls_v1_2_cipher_suites.description: The encryption algorithms available for TLS 1.2 client connections, specified as a colon-separated list in OpenSSL format. Use this to support older clients that require specific encryption methods.

tls_v1_3_cipher_suites.name: tls_v1_3_cipher_suites
tls_v1_3_cipher_suites.description: The encryption algorithms available for TLS 1.3 client connections, specified as a colon-separated list in OpenSSL format. Most deployments don't need to change this. Only modify it to meet specific organizational security requirements.

tombstone_retention_ms.name: tombstone_retention_ms
tombstone_retention_ms.description:
The retention time for tombstone records and transaction markers in a compacted topic. Redpanda removes them after the retention limit is exceeded.

For topics that use Tiered Storage v1, tombstone removal is silently skipped while any of `cloud_storage_enabled`, `cloud_storage_enable_remote_read`, or `cloud_storage_enable_remote_write` is enabled: the configuration is accepted, but tombstones are not removed for the topic. This restriction does not apply to topics that use Tiered Storage v2, available starting in Redpanda 26.2.

If not set, tombstone removal is disabled.

topic_fds_per_partition.name: topic_fds_per_partition
topic_fds_per_partition.description: File descriptors required per partition replica. If topic creation results in the ratio of file descriptor limit to partition replicas being lower than this value, creation of new topics is fails.

topic_label_aggregation_limit.name: topic_label_aggregation_limit
topic_label_aggregation_limit.description: When the number of topics exceeds this limit, the topic label in generated metrics will be aggregated. If `null`, then there is no limit.

topic_memory_per_partition.name: topic_memory_per_partition
topic_memory_per_partition.description: Required memory in bytes per partition replica when creating or altering topics. The total size of the memory pool for partitions is the total memory available to Redpanda times topic_partitions_memory_allocation_percent, and then each partition created requires topic_memory_per_partition bytes from that pool. If insufficent memory is available, topic creation or alternation will fail.

topic_partitions_memory_allocation_perce.name: topic_partitions_memory_allocation_percent
topic_partitions_memory_allocation_perce.description: Percentage of total memory to reserve for topic partitions. See `topic_memory_per_partition` for details.

topic_partitions_per_shard.name: topic_partitions_per_shard
topic_partitions_per_shard.description: Maximum number of partition replicas per shard. If topic creation results in the ratio of partition replicas to shards being higher than this value, creation of new topics fails.

topic_partitions_reserve_shard0.name: topic_partitions_reserve_shard0
topic_partitions_reserve_shard0.description: Reserved partition slots on shard (CPU core) 0 on each node. If this is greater than or equal to `topic_partitions_per_shard`, no data partitions will be scheduled on shard 0.

transaction_coordinator_cleanup_policy.name: transaction_coordinator_cleanup_policy
transaction_coordinator_cleanup_policy.description: Cleanup policy for a transaction coordinator topic.

transaction_coordinator_delete_retention.name: transaction_coordinator_delete_retention_ms
transaction_coordinator_delete_retention.description:
Delete segments older than this age. To ensure transaction state is retained for as long as the longest-running transaction, make sure this is greater than or equal to `transactional_id_expiration_ms`.

For example, if your typical transactions run for one hour, consider setting both `transaction_coordinator_delete_retention_ms` and `transactional_id_expiration_ms` to at least 3600000 (one hour), or a little over.

transaction_coordinator_log_segment_size.name: transaction_coordinator_log_segment_size
transaction_coordinator_log_segment_size.description: The size (in bytes) each log segment should be.

transaction_coordinator_partitions.name: transaction_coordinator_partitions
transaction_coordinator_partitions.description: Number of partitions for transactions coordinator.

transaction_max_timeout_ms.name: transaction_max_timeout_ms
transaction_max_timeout_ms.description: The maximum allowed timeout for transactions. If a client-requested transaction timeout exceeds this configuration, the broker returns an error during transactional producer initialization. This guardrail prevents hanging transactions from blocking consumer progress.

transactional_id_expiration_ms.name: transactional_id_expiration_ms
transactional_id_expiration_ms.description:
Expiration time of producer IDs for both transactional and idempotent producers. Despite the name, this setting applies to all producer types. Measured starting from the time of the last write until now for a given ID.

Producer IDs are automatically removed from memory when they expire, which helps manage memory usage. However, this natural cleanup may not be sufficient for workloads with high producer churn rates. Tune this value based on your application's producer session and transaction lifetimes. Consider your longest-running transaction duration plus a buffer to avoid premature expiration.

tx_log_stats_interval_s.name: tx_log_stats_interval_s
tx_log_stats_interval_s.description: How often to log per partition tx stats, works only with debug logging enabled.

tx_timeout_delay_ms.name: tx_timeout_delay_ms
tx_timeout_delay_ms.description: Delay before scheduling the next check for timed out transactions.

unsafe_enable_consumer_offsets_delete_re.name: unsafe_enable_consumer_offsets_delete_retention
unsafe_enable_consumer_offsets_delete_re.description: Enables delete retention of consumer offsets topic. This is an internal-only configuration and should be enabled only after consulting with Redpanda support.

upgrade_override_checks.name: upgrade_override_checks
upgrade_override_checks.description: Whether to violate safety checks when starting a Redpanda version newer than the cluster's consensus version.

usage_disk_persistance_interval_sec.name: usage_disk_persistance_interval_sec
usage_disk_persistance_interval_sec.description: The interval in which all usage stats are written to disk.

usage_num_windows.name: usage_num_windows
usage_num_windows.description: The number of windows to persist in memory and disk.

usage_window_width_interval_sec.name: usage_window_width_interval_sec
usage_window_width_interval_sec.description: The width of a usage window, tracking cloud and kafka ingress/egress traffic each interval.

use_fetch_scheduler_group.name: use_fetch_scheduler_group
use_fetch_scheduler_group.description: Use a separate scheduler group for fetch processing.

use_kafka_handler_scheduler_group.name: use_kafka_handler_scheduler_group
use_kafka_handler_scheduler_group.description: Use a separate scheduler group to handle parsing Kafka protocol requests.

use_produce_scheduler_group.name: use_produce_scheduler_group
use_produce_scheduler_group.description: Use a separate scheduler group to process Kafka produce requests.

verbose_logging_timeout_sec_max.name: verbose_logging_timeout_sec_max
verbose_logging_timeout_sec_max.description: Maximum duration in seconds for verbose (`TRACE` or `DEBUG`) logging. Values configured above this will be clamped. If null (the default) there is no limit. Can be overridden in the Admin API on a per-request basis.

virtual_cluster_min_producer_ids.name: virtual_cluster_min_producer_ids
virtual_cluster_min_producer_ids.description: Minimum number of active producers per virtual cluster.

write.caching.name: write.caching
write.caching.description:
The write caching mode to apply to a topic.

When `write.caching` is set, it overrides the cluster property `write_caching_default`. Write caching acknowledges a message as soon as it is received and acknowledged on a majority of brokers, without waiting for it to be written to disk. With `acks=all`, this provides lower latency while still ensuring that a majority of brokers acknowledge the write. Fsyncs follow `flush.ms` and `flush.bytes`, whichever is reached first.

write_caching_default.name: write_caching_default
write_caching_default.description:
The default write caching mode to apply to user topics. Write caching acknowledges a message as soon as it is received and acknowledged on a majority of brokers, without waiting for it to be written to disk. With `acks=all`, this provides lower latency while still ensuring that a majority of brokers acknowledge the write. 

Fsyncs follow `raft_replica_max_pending_flush_bytes` and `raft_replica_max_flush_delay_ms`, whichever is reached first.

The `write_caching_default` cluster property can be overridden with the `write.caching` topic property.

zstd_decompress_workspace_bytes.name: zstd_decompress_workspace_bytes
zstd_decompress_workspace_bytes.description: Size of the zstd decompression workspace.
